subject: Priv infra componentization and evidence request — next steps
messages:
From: Sophie James <sophie.james@acmehealth.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: Paul Grant <pgrant@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: Priv infra componentization + evidence bundle request

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed with our security and procurement teams, Acme needs three things to proceed with the procurement: a high-level map that shows how Redwood's private deployment components will live inside our VPC (network zones, egress paths, bastion/management plane), a proposed split of Terraform/Helm/Ansible responsibilities (who owns which artifacts), and a compact evidence bundle we can attach to our vendor security form (basic SOC 2 pointers + where to find module signing attestations).

Can your team produce a short component map and a suggested module interface (TF + Helm value schema + Ansible runbooks) we can review by next Wednesday (2026-11-11)? We also need an exportable artifact we can share with our audit team (PDF or ZIP).

Sophie
Sophie James
Lead IT Security, Acme Health Systems

[Attachment: acs-evidence-request-form.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sophie James <sophie.james@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-08T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv infra componentization + evidence bundle request

Hi Sophie —

Thanks — looping in the infra leads. We can deliver a concise package by 2026-11-11; I want to be explicit about scope so we don't over-index on low-value artifacts. Proposed deliverables: 1) one-slide component map (PDF + spreadsheet) showing VPC zones, peering, NAT/egress, and management access; 2) a "module responsibilities" table that maps Terraform modules, Helm charts, and Ansible playbooks (owners + public interfaces); 3) a zipped evidence bundle that points to where we keep signing provenance and CI run logs (we will not include full logs, we will provide redacted pointers).

We will attach a short compatibility note for your SOC/arch reviewers describing our module signing and artifact retention. Does that match what your security team expects? If so I will tag work items and share an initial draft by EOD Monday (11/09).

Best —
Priya Natarajan
Director, Private Deployments (Redwood Inference)

[Attachment: priv-iac-component-map.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Priv infra componentization + evidence bundle request

Priya — forwarding Sophie for visibility. Couple of operational notes that should be included in the deliverable:

- CI gate evidence: include the link to the pipeline that runs module vetting (we can provide the audit view, not full secrets).
- TF module interfaces: prefer a small, stable public inputs file (tfvars schema) rather than many tiny modules that leak complexity into customers.
- Helm: include a values-schema.md and an example overlay for Acme's constrained subnets.
- Ansible: keep runbooks idempotent and reference the tuning playbook we use for bastion/ssh hardening.

Rishi/Marcus — can you draft the module responsibilities doc and attach the minimal diff that shows the proposed new input variables? I put a soft blocker on anything that would require cross-module backwards-incompatible changes for existing customers.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Engineering

[Attachment: tf-module-proposal.diff (text/x-diff)]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Priv infra componentization + evidence bundle request

Folks —

Attached is a compact patch that sketches the interface changes I'm proposing (namespaced variables, outputs for external IPs and service endpoints, and an opt-in module signing check in the root CI). Notes:

- Backwards compatibility: all changes are opt-in via a new tfvar (enable_componentized=true). Existing stacks unaffected.
- Helm overlays: we add a small chart values-schema.md and a test overlay for Acme to demonstrate subnet constraints.
- Evidence: I included a short README describing how to extract a signed artifact from our artifact registry; the full signing chain is accessible via a redacted path in the evidence bundle.

I'll push a PR to the priv-iac repo and drop the link into this thread when it's ready. Happy to walk Sophie/Paul through the patch if they'd like a 30m sync.

-rishi
Senior Infra Eng
[Attachment: brief-evidence-readme.txt (text/plain)]

From: Paul Grant <pgrant@acmehealth.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: Sophie James <sophie.james@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv infra componentization + evidence bundle request

Priya —

This looks good, thanks. Sophie and I reviewed the proposed scope and the opt-in compatibility approach addresses our main concern. Please go ahead and deliver the component map, the TF/Helm/Ansible responsibilities table, and the zipped evidence bundle. Procurement will need the PDF of the component map and the DocuSign link for the updated annex (I put procurement on CC).

If you can get the deliverables to us by close of day tomorrow (2026-11-11), we will open the purchase order.

Paul Grant
Head of Procurement, Acme Health Systems
